Protein-RNA binding models: what transfers to new proteins

Draft, 2026-10-30, repository commit 3053e53. Every number is traceable to EXPERIMENT_LOG.md or a results file; single-seed results are marked. Sections: 1 data and baselines, 2 evaluation design, 3 transfer to new proteins, 4 attempts and controls, 5 in vivo data, 6 affinity, 7 not done. M = method, H = hypothesis, I = illustration.

0. Task, design and terms

Question of this report: do models that receive the protein sequence predict RNA binding for proteins that were not used for training, or do they use only RNA composition and the similarity of the protein to training proteins? All results below are measured on in vitro data unless section 5 says otherwise.

TermMeaning
TaskPredict whether a protein binds an RNA sequence. Each example is a (protein sequence, RNA sequence) pair with a label: binds = 1, does not bind = 0.
Data sourcesIn vitro binding experiments on 494 RNA-binding proteins: HTR-SELEX and RBNS (selection of RNAs from random pools, RNAs of 20-40 nt), RNAcompete (fixed RNA probes with measured intensities). In vivo data (section 5): eCLIP / CLIP peaks in cells (101-nt windows).
v3aThe in vitro dataset (2.66 million pairs) split into train / validation / test by protein name. Related proteins (homologs) of a test protein can be in the training set.
v3bThe same pairs re-split by homology clusters: proteins that are similar in sequence (identity >= 40% over >= 50% of the sequence, MMseqs2) always fall on the same side. Test proteins have no close relative in training (160 clusters; 375 / 55 / 64 proteins in train / validation / test).
Standard testTest pairs as labelled by the assay. Negatives are other RNAs of the same experiment, so RNA composition alone is informative.
Cross-protein probeTest built to require the protein: the same RNA is a positive for protein A and a negative for another protein B of the same assay (schematic above). RNA-only models score 0.5.
AUROCArea under the ROC curve: probability that a random positive is scored above a random negative. 0.5 = chance, 1.0 = perfect. Intervals in brackets are 95% intervals from resampling proteins (protein-level bootstrap).
SpearmanRank correlation between two lists of numbers (1 = same ranking, 0 = unrelated).
V2Neural network (convolutional, CNN) with one branch for the RNA sequence and one for the protein sequence (both one-hot encoded); the two vectors are concatenated and classified.
V4Same as V2 but the RNA and protein vectors also pass through a bilinear (multiplicative) layer so that the network can model their interaction.
Frozen-embedding headSmall neural network on top of fixed vectors from large pretrained models: ESM-2 (protein language model) and RNA-FM (RNA language model). Variants: RNA only, protein only, concatenation, bilinear.
Nearest-protein baseline (nn1)No protein model. For every training protein an RNA-only model (logistic regression on k-mer frequencies) is fitted; a test pair is scored with the RNA model of the training protein whose sequence is most similar to the test protein.
RNA priorMean of the RNA-only models of all training proteins; ignores the test protein.
Seen / unseen proteinSeen: the protein was in the training data. Unseen: it was not; in v3b additionally no close relative was.
Identity binBest sequence identity of a test protein to any training protein (MMseqs2), grouped into <30% / no hit, 30-50%, 50-70%, 70-90%, >=90%.
Pfam, RRM, KHPfam: database of protein domain families. RRM and KH are the most common RNA-binding domain families.
SeedRandom initialisation of training; results over several seeds show the run-to-run spread.
PaRPI, eCLIP, icSHAPEPaRPI: published method and benchmark of 261 in vivo binding datasets (eCLIP and related CLIP data). eCLIP: protein-RNA crosslinking experiment in cells. icSHAPE: in vivo RNA structure probing.

Main results

  1. On the name-level split (v3a), V4 (CNN with a bilinear protein-RNA layer) reaches AUROC 0.754 on the cross-protein probe. This tracks the sequence identity of the test protein to training proteins (0.52 without a homolog, 0.88 at >= 70% identity), and the nearest-protein baseline, which contains no protein model, reaches 0.746.
  2. After removing homologs (v3b), the nearest-protein baseline scores 0.627; V2 / V4 (CNNs trained on one-hot sequences) score 0.527 / 0.559 and heads on frozen ESM-2 + RNA-FM embeddings 0.50-0.56 (3 seeds). Adding the heads to the baseline raises the score by 0.004.
  3. The same frozen-embedding heads reach 0.83 on proteins seen in training with new RNAs: training works, transfer to unseen homology clusters does not.
  4. The standard test is solvable from the RNA alone (RNA-only head 0.651 on the standard test, 0.500 on the probe). Classic RPI benchmarks behave similarly.
  5. Predicting a protein's RNA motif from its sequence is not better than the average motif (ridge regression on ESM-2: Spearman 0.179 vs 0.155); the measured motif would give 0.90.
  6. For proteins with in vivo data, k-mer models trained on eCLIP score the same protein's in vitro RNAs at 0.67 (RNA prior 0.58, in vitro own data 0.95).

1. Data and baselines

M1 Data and splits

Method. MMseqs2 best identity of every test protein to the training proteins (script 55); v3b = clusters by single linkage (identity >=40% at coverage >=50%, or >=70% at >=10%).

v3a (split by protein name)v3b (split by homology cluster)
proteins / pairs494 / 2.66 M (HTR-SELEX, RBNS, RNAcompete)same pairs, re-split: 160 clusters; train 375, val 55, test 64 proteins
test proteins >=50% identical to training62% (7 are >=90%)3% (none >=70%)
test proteins at 30-50% identity15 of 5553 of 64
shared protein names / sequences with training1 / 1 (test)0 / 0
test rows whose RNA also occurs in training69%73% (assay probe sets are reused across proteins)

Domain-level similarity at 30-50% remains for most v3b test proteins and cannot be removed inside RRM (at 30% identity all RRM proteins merge into one cluster of 400+).

Caveats

Greedy clustering left near-identical proteins on both sides (e.g. PABPC1 / PABPC4), hence single linkage.

M2 Baselines

Method. Each baseline uses a different piece of information. The nearest-protein baseline fits a k-mer logistic regression on the RNAs of every training protein and scores a test pair with the model of the most similar training protein (MMseqs2).

BaselineInformation usedv3a probev3b probev3b standard test
RNA priorRNA only (mean of all training protein models)0.500 [0.45, 0.55]0.500 [0.46, 0.54]0.591 [0.55, 0.63]
RNA-only neural head (RNA-FM)RNA only-0.5000.651
protein-only neural head (ESM-2)protein only-0.5040.507
nearest protein, k-mer LR (nn1)sequence similarity to training proteins + their RNAs0.724 [0.66, 0.77]0.627 [0.57, 0.68]0.676 [0.61, 0.74]
top-3 neighbours (nn3)same, 3 neighbours0.746 [0.70, 0.79]0.607 [0.54, 0.67]0.644 [0.58, 0.72]
per-protein model on its own data (seen protein)the protein's own labelled RNAs, honest 60/20/20 split0.83 (seen protein, new RNAs, frozen head)-median 0.95 (HTR-SELEX), 1.00 (RBNS), 0.99 (RNAcompete)

Brackets: 95% interval, protein-level bootstrap. The seen-protein row is the ceiling for a protein with its own data.

Caveats

'Cross-protein probe': the same RNA paired with another protein of the same assay where it is not a positive; RNA composition is identical in positives and negatives, so RNA-only and GC baselines give 0.500.

2. Evaluation design

H1 The standard test can be solved from the RNA alone supported

Test. Neural heads on frozen embeddings with RNA only, protein only, or both (script 67, 3 seeds); same models on the standard test and on the probe.

Caveats

73% of test rows share an RNA with training rows. Single v3b split.

H2 Classic RPI benchmarks can be solved from one molecule supported

Test. RPISeq-style random forest with RNA-only, protein-only and combined features on RPI369/488/1446/2241 (script 60).

Caveats

Our re-implementation does not reproduce the published numbers (RPI369 random 0.974 vs 0.85 reported); the claim concerns dataset properties only. De-duplicated pairs, untuned forest.

4. Attempts to improve transfer; controls

H6 The null result on new clusters is caused by a pipeline defect ruled out

Test. Positive control: 5% of the training RNAs (all rows containing them) are held out; a cross-protein probe is built from them for the seen proteins.

CheckResult
seen proteins, new RNAs (ordinary labels / cross-protein negatives)0.828 / 0.827
unseen clusters, same runs0.550 / 0.542
nearest protein recomputed inside the hybrid pipelineprobe 0.6265, standard 0.6755 (script 59: 0.627 / 0.676)
protein shuffled at test (bilinear heads)0.55 -> 0.48 and 0.57 -> 0.50
Caveats

Shows the head can learn protein-specific preferences; does not prove that no architecture can generalise.

H7 Frozen ESM-2 / RNA-FM embeddings, combination with the baseline and tuning improve transfer to new clusters not supported

Test. Heads rna / protein / concat / bilinear (3 seeds), joint hybrid, held-out stacking, hyper-parameter sweep (scripts 67, 71).

Scorerprobe (mean +/- sd, 3 seeds)standard test
RNA-only head0.500 +/- 0.0000.651 +/- 0.001
protein-only head0.504 +/- 0.0040.507 +/- 0.001
concat head0.528 +/- 0.0060.618 +/- 0.009
bilinear head, ordinary labels0.531 +/- 0.0270.623 +/- 0.032
bilinear head + cross-protein negatives0.559 +/- 0.0100.531 +/- 0.015
nn1 + head, weights fitted on val (seed 42)0.6300.676
joint hybrid, trained together (seed 42)0.5570.533

Stack weights: nn1 0.137, head 0.012. In the joint hybrid the nn weight collapsed 1.0 -> 0.14 while the head memorised training proteins. Sweep (probe, seed 42; default 0.570): lr 3e-4 / 3e-3 0.544 / 0.557, hidden 128 / 512 0.539 / 0.549, dropout 0.1 / 0.5 0.529 / 0.556; weight-decay variants pending.

Caveats

Mean pooling over the whole protein dilutes domain signal (RBD-cropped pooling not tested). Best epochs of the heads are 1-5.

H8 Training with composition-neutral cross-protein negatives yields transfer to new clusters not supported

Test. Each training positive is paired with the same RNA and another training protein of the same assay (script 65 for V4, script 67 for frozen heads).

One-hot V4: training loss 1.36 -> 0.77 while the validation probe stays at 0.49-0.52 (early stop at epoch 10, best 0.522). Frozen head: +0.03 on the probe, and the standard-test AUROC drops from 0.623 to 0.531 because the RNA shortcut is removed.

Caveats

One seed for V4 and one set of hyper-parameters for the one-hot model.

H9 Transfer increases with the number of training clusters partly

Test. Bilinear head with cross-protein negatives on 25/50/75/100% of the 160 clusters (two seeds per fraction, three at 100%).

Caveats

The one large cluster (220 RRM proteins) dominates sampling, so fractions are not comparable in protein count.

H10 The RNA motif of a new protein can be predicted from its sequence not supported

Test. Target: per-protein 5-mer log2 enrichment (1024 values); ESM-2 mean embedding; ridge and kNN; Spearman on 64 test proteins; probe AUROC when RNAs are scored with the predicted profile (script 73).

H15 The same protein has concordant eCLIP and in vitro specificity partly

Test. 50 proteins present in PaRPI eCLIP data and in v3b (in vitro rows only); k-mer LR on eCLIP vs genomic negatives or vs other RBPs' peaks (script 74).

Scorermean [95% CI over proteins]median
